items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: I had to learn, even from high school Richard Wagner and Strauss and Beethoven and all these things

ctx.x: The improvisation you see is a state of mind. You have to kind of be, well you have to assume the attitude of having or exercising the liberty to do that. We all have the liberty but we don’t always exercise it. And I mean Charlie Parker came to my house to get his horn fixed, and Gene Ammons and Johnny Griffin were my father’s students. So you’re listening to them and they come in and, you know Sonny Stitt would come from out of town, “I’ve got to get my horn fixed.” And everybody was rotating through there. And

the discussion was more about the transference from swing into bebop because a lot of the older musicians had an attitude about the beboppers, you know, they thought that a lot of them were not able to play. They hadn’t encountered — well Bird of course had that prodigious technique, and Dizzy Gillespie, and quite a few people around, but that was not common. You know a lot of people were just well I can’t do this so I’ll do that. You know, but I never had any doubt that all of these musics were legitimate. And I…
Um hum. Just as a performing musician.
